worked_example.problem: Today is {ddmmyyyy(d1, m1, y1)}. A tin of milk says “Use before {ddmmyyyy(d2, m2, y2)}”. Can we still use it?
steps: Compare the dates: first the year, then the month, then the day.
The use-before date, {ddmmyyyy(d2, m2, y2)}, is before today, {ddmmyyyy(d1, m1, y1)}.
worked_example.answer: No: it has expired. Do not use it.

cards.idea: Hazard symbols warn of danger. A flame means flammable; a skull and crossbones means toxic.
example: Kerosene has the flame symbol: keep it away from fire.

cards.idea: A label tells how to use and store a product, warnings, who made it and the expiry date.
example: “Keep out of reach of children” is a warning.

cards.idea: Never use a product after its expiry (“use before”) date.
example: Today {ddmmyyyy(d1, m1, y1)}; use before {ddmmyyyy(d2, m2, y2)}: still good.
checks: stillGood(d1, m1, y1, d2, m2, y2)

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: The flame symbol means the product catches fire easily.
Read the label before using a product.
Keep dangerous products away from children.

wrong.text: It is fine to keep kerosene in a drink bottle.
wrong.explain: Someone could drink it by mistake. Keep it in its own labelled container.

wrong.text: A product is still good after its expiry date.
